evals.prompt: Review three DynamoDB proposals from our backend PR: (1) use `UpdateTable` to change `OrdersByStatusGSI` in place from `KEYS_ONLY` to `ALL`; (2) if that fails, pass both `Delete` and `Create` for `OrdersByStatusGSI` in a single `UpdateTable` call; and (3) pass `ConditionExpression='tenant_id = :tid'` on `GetItem` to stop cross-tenant reads.
evals.expected_output: Rejects all three misconceptions using exact DynamoDB axioms: (1) **GSI `Projection` (and `KeySchema`) is immutable** after creation — `UpdateTable` cannot alter an existing GSI's projection; (2) a single `UpdateTable` call accepts **at most one GSI operation** (one `Create` OR one `Delete`), and dropping first creates a read outage — instead use an **additive migration** (create `OrdersByStatusV2` with `ProjectionType=ALL` -> wait for `ACTIVE` backfill -> cut reads over -> delete old GSI); and (3) **`ConditionExpression` is write-only** (`PutItem`/`UpdateItem`/`DeleteItem`/`TransactWriteItems`) — `GetItem`/`Query`/`Scan` do NOT support conditional reads or throw `ConditionalCheckFailedException`; enforce tenant isolation by making `tenant_id` part of the table's partition key (plus IAM `dynamodb:LeadingKeys`).
expectations: Activates the amazon-dynamodb skill

Explains that GSI `Projection` is immutable and `UpdateTable` allows only one GSI operation per call, prescribing an additive new-GSI migration (`Create` new GSI -> `ACTIVE` -> cutover -> `Delete` old)
Explains that `ConditionExpression` is write-side only (`GetItem` has no conditional read) and recommends partition-keying by tenant ID (`dynamodb:LeadingKeys`) for tenant isolation

evals.prompt: Fact-check four cost optimizations our team wants to ship on DynamoDB: (1) toggle our table between `PAY_PER_REQUEST` and `PROVISIONED` every 2 hours for daytime peaks; (2) buy DynamoDB Reserved Capacity for our On-Demand tables; (3) wrap single-item optimistic-locking `UpdateItem` calls in `TransactWriteItems` for atomicity; and (4) ignore failed `ConditionExpression` retries in WCU math because failed checks are free.
evals.expected_output: Corrects all four errors directly: (1) capacity-mode switches have a **24-hour cooldown** (at most once per 24 hours per table); (2) **Reserved Capacity applies ONLY to `PROVISIONED` capacity**, never On-Demand (`PAY_PER_REQUEST` — use Standard-IA or provisioned+autoscaling+RC instead); (3) single-item `UpdateItem`/`PutItem`/`DeleteItem` with `ConditionExpression` is **already atomic**, and wrapping it in `TransactWriteItems` doubles (`2x`) WCU/WRU cost for zero benefit; and (4) **`ConditionalCheckFailedException` consumes the full WCU/WRU** of the item write.
expectations: Activates the amazon-dynamodb skill
Corrects the 24-hour capacity-mode switch cooldown and confirms Reserved Capacity applies exclusively to `PROVISIONED` mode (never On-Demand)
Confirms single-item `UpdateItem` with `ConditionExpression` is already atomic (`TransactWriteItems` wastes 2x WCU) and `ConditionalCheckFailedException` still bills full write capacity

evals.prompt: Can Amazon DynamoDB run approximate nearest-neighbor vector search natively on our product catalog items without syncing to OpenSearch, how is the index configured and queried, and what happens to search results when a user edits a product's description text?
evals.expected_output: Confirms **DynamoDB has native vector search** via `VectorIndexes` on `CreateTable` / `VectorIndexUpdates` on `UpdateTable` and queried via **`SearchVectors`** (`boto3 >= 1.43.64` / AWS CLI v2 `>= 2.36.16`): (1) requires **On-Demand (`PAY_PER_REQUEST`)** capacity and is a distinct index type (NOT a GSI; `Query`, `Scan`, PartiQL, and DAX are rejected on vector indexes); (2) `Dimensions`, `DistanceFunction`, `Projection`, and `SearchSchema` are **all immutable**; and (3) **DynamoDB NEVER auto-recomputes embeddings** when item text is edited — stale vectors persist silently until the application re-embeds with the same model synchronously on write or asynchronously via DynamoDB Streams.
expectations: Activates the amazon-dynamodb skill
Explains native `VectorIndexes` + `SearchVectors` (`boto3 >= 1.43.64`), On-Demand requirement, immutable index attributes, and that `Query`/`Scan`/PartiQL/DAX do not work against a vector index
Explicitly warns that editing item text does NOT auto-refresh embeddings and prescribes synchronous re-embedding or a DynamoDB Streams re-embedding consumer

evals.prompt: Design a DynamoDB data model for a multi-tenant B2B SaaS (`500` RPS reads, `120` RPS writes) supporting: (A) fetch tenant workspace metadata, (B) list latest 50 invoices for a tenant sorted by `created_at`, (C) look up an invoice by external `stripe_invoice_id`, and (D) bulk-import 200 line items where some items have 600 KB PDF blobs attached.
evals.expected_output: Builds the explicit **access-pattern list** first (RPS, item size, consistency), keys partitions by `TENANT#<id>` (`PK`) + `INVOICE#<iso_ts>#<inv_id>` (`SK`) with a sparse/targeted GSI on `stripe_invoice_id`, flags the **`400 KB` hard item size limit** (storing `600 KB` PDFs in S3 with an S3 URI pointer in DynamoDB — noting `1 MB` is the `Query` page limit, not item limit), and uses chunked `BatchWriteItem` (`<= 25` items / `16 MB` per batch) with exponential-backoff retries on **`UnprocessedItems`** because `BatchWriteItem` is NOT atomic.

Enforces the `400 KB` max item size cap by offloading `600 KB` PDF blobs to S3 and designs tenant-scoped `PK`/`SK` + `stripe_invoice_id` GSI
Handles 200-item bulk imports via chunked 25-item `BatchWriteItem` calls with exponential backoff on `UnprocessedItems` (noting non-atomicity)

evals.prompt: Calculate the monthly DynamoDB cost in `us-east-1` for an On-Demand table storing `2,500 GB` of order history (`2 KB` average item size, `1` GSI projecting `ALL` attributes) with `15 million` eventually consistent reads and `5 million` writes per month. Should this table use `STANDARD` or `STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS` (`Standard-IA`)?
evals.expected_output: Computes storage (`2,500 GB` base + `2,500 GB` GSI = `5,000 GB` total) plus On-Demand RRU (`0.5 RRU` per `4 KB` eventually consistent read) and WRU (`2 WRU` base + `2 WRU` GSI per `2 KB` write) across both `STANDARD` (`$0.25/GB-mo` storage vs lower RRU/WRU) and `STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS` (`$0.10/GB-mo` — 60% cheaper storage vs ~25% higher RRU/WRU), demonstrating clearly that storage dominates (`$1,250/mo` vs `$500/mo` storage) so **`STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS` saves ~$700+/month**.
expectations: Activates the amazon-dynamodb skill
Accounts for both base table and `ALL`-projected GSI storage (`5,000 GB` total) and write amplification (`2 KB` = `2 WRU` base + `2 WRU` GSI per write)
Compares `STANDARD` vs `STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS` monthly totals and recommends `Standard-IA` because storage cost dominates low-throughput reads/writes

evals.prompt: Architect a zero-data-loss DynamoDB TTL archival pipeline to S3/Parquet using DynamoDB Streams: which stream view type, iterator type, retention window, ESM failure controls, and filter criteria prevent dropping expired records while ignoring ordinary user updates?
evals.expected_output: Configures `StreamViewType=OLD_IMAGE` (or `NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES`), clarifies DynamoDB Streams has a **24-hour retention window** and supports iterator types **`TRIM_HORIZON` and `LATEST` only** (never Kinesis `AT_TIMESTAMP`), applies a free Event Source Mapping `FilterCriteria` matching system TTL deletes (`eventName: ["REMOVE"]` + `userIdentity.principalId: ["dynamodb.amazonaws.com"]`), and configures `BisectBatchOnFunctionError=true` + SQS/S3 `OnFailure` destination + idempotent S3/Firehose delivery before the 24h window expires (noting TTL deletion occurs asynchronously up to ~48h after epoch seconds).
expectations: Activates the amazon-dynamodb skill
Specifies `OLD_IMAGE`/`NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES`, 24-hour stream retention, and `TRIM_HORIZON`/`LATEST` iterator semantics
Filters ESM events to system TTL `REMOVE` (`dynamodb.amazonaws.com`) with `BisectBatchOnFunctionError` and an `OnFailure` DLQ destination

evals.prompt: Our On-Demand DynamoDB table has plenty of account-level quota, yet bursts to a single `status = 'PENDING'` GSI partition throw `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` on `PutItem` calls to the base table. Explain the root cause and concrete fix.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses **per-partition physical throughput limits (`1,000 WRU/s` write / `3,000 RRU/s` read per partition)** combined with **GSI write backpressure**: even on On-Demand tables, funneling >1,000 WRU/s into a single GSI partition key (`status = 'PENDING'`) exhausts that GSI partition's buffer and throttles base-table `PutItem`/`UpdateItem` writes! Recommends enabling **CloudWatch Contributor Insights**, replacing low-cardinality `status` PK with **write-sharded composite keys** (`PENDING#<0..N>` or bucketing by time/shard via an additive new GSI migration), and keeping projections sparse/minimal.
expectations: Activates the amazon-dynamodb skill
Identifies the `1,000 WRU/s` (`3,000 RRU/s`) per-partition physical limit and explains how hot GSI partition backpressure throttles base-table writes
Prescribes CloudWatch Contributor Insights + additive write-sharded GSI migration (`PENDING#<shard>` / sparse GSI) because GSI `KeySchema` is immutable

evals.prompt: Verify via AWS documentation MCP tools how **DynamoDB Warm Throughput** pre-warming works for sudden flash-sale launches and how **Global Tables Multi-Region Strong Consistency (MRSC)** differs from Multi-Region Eventual Consistency (MREC).
evals.expected_output: Consults `awsknowledge` / `aws-mcp` documentation tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands and confirms: (1) **Warm Throughput** (`WarmThroughput` on `CreateTable`/`UpdateTable` for base tables and GSIs) pre-scales `ReadUnitsPerSecond` and `WriteUnitsPerSecond` upfront so flash sales don't hit cold-table adaptive scaling throttling, and cannot be dialed down below current pre-warmed capacity; and (2) **Global Tables MRSC** provides `RPO = 0` strong cross-region reads/writes across a 3-Region architecture (3 full replicas or 2 replicas + 1 witness Region, with no GSIs/LSIs/Streams caveats per docs) vs **MREC** asynchronous last-writer-wins replication.
expectations: Activates the amazon-dynamodb skill and consults `awsknowledge` / `aws-mcp` documentation tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands
Explains `WarmThroughput` (`ReadUnitsPerSecond`/`WriteUnitsPerSecond`) pre-warming on base tables and GSIs
